findings.title: Migration plan omits the agents-tree drift guard as a consumer of the analysis-skill move
findings.description: Line 182 lists the move's consumers as `DELIVERIES[AGENTS].bundle_subdirs`, `bundled_skill_names`, and "the fixtures in `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py` and `tests/skills/test_targets.py`," and line 184 claims existing tests for those commands "pass without edits other than the moved fixture paths." That is not true for the most load-bearing test on this path: `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py::_claude_twins()` pairs every file under the Claude `bundle_subdirs` (`sq/`, `analysis/`) with `commands/agents/<sub>-<stem>/SKILL.md` via `_agents_root() = get_commands_source()/"agents"`, and `test_every_claude_command_has_an_agents_twin` / `test_openai_yaml_mirrors_disable_model_invocation` read the analysis skills from exactly that location — not from fixtures. Moving `analysis-understand/` and `analysis-tech-debt-audit/` to `commands/analysis/agents/` breaks both tests, and the fix requires teaching the 925 drift guard (whose docstring calls the two trees "a bijection") to search a second root — an edit the design never schedules, in step 2 ("D4 move … confirm criterion 7") or anywhere else. D4 (line 132) similarly asserts "Nothing else reads `commands/analysis/` recursively" and enumerates runtime readers, but does not acknowledge the test-side resolver whose whole job is finding these skills in the old location. Secondary, same claim: `check_skill_packs`'s signature must change to loop targets, while `tests/cli/test_doctor_checks.py:406-433` call it as `check_skill_packs(commands_dir=…, cwd=…)` — either those tests change or the design must state that `commands_dir` still overrides the per-target root resolution. Add both to the migration consumer list so the "behavior preserved" claim is accurate.

findings.title: D8's "like commands" analogy does not hold at the `run_all_checks` call site
findings.description: `check_skill_packs` is to iterate `_command_targets_to_check(None)`, but command rows get their targets from `run_all_checks(ide=…)` (setup passes its selected target; `doctor_checks.py:631` loops `_command_targets_to_check(ide)`). Hardcoding `None` inside the skill-pack check means `sq setup --ide codex` shows only the Claude skill-pack row unless the Codex CLI happens to be on PATH at that moment — a weaker form of "per target, like commands" than the section title claims. The choice is stated, not hidden, and skill-pack rows are indeed not setup-table keys, so this is likely fine; but the design should say explicitly that setup's skill-pack view is deliberately doctor's default view rather than setup's target, so the asymmetry with the command rows is a decision and not an oversight.

findings.title: "one line each" understates the `sq model list` fix
findings.description: Each named file carries three occurrences of `sq model list`, not one: `commands/sq/review.md` lines 60, 112, 158 and `commands/agents/sq-review/SKILL.md` lines 82, 134, 180. The fix is trivial either way, but "one line each" (and success criterion 9's "both `review` command files say `sq models list`") invites an implementer to change only the first hit and leave two stale references per file. Correct the count so the sweep is complete.
